title: Converting a Partnership Firm to an LLP: Step-by-Step Legal Roadmap & Tax Exemption Under Section 47
author: CA Swetha SV
excerpt: A comprehensive practitioner guide to converting Indian Partnership Act 1932 firms into Limited Liability Partnerships under the Second Schedule of LLP Act 2008, ensuring 100% tax neutrality under Section 47(xiiib).
summary: This whitepaper breaks down the legal, procedural, and tax steps for converting a partnership firm into an LLP, detailing ROC filing sequences, MCA forms, capital gains exemptions, stamp duty, and GST ITC migration.
content:
### 1. Introduction: Why Traditional Partnerships Must Evolve

For decades, the partnership firm registered under the **Indian Partnership Act, 1932** was the default vehicle of choice for family enterprises, professional consultants, traders, and manufacturing units across India. However, traditional partnerships carry a fatal structural flaw: **unlimited personal liability**.

Under Section 25 of the Partnership Act, 1932, every partner is jointly and severally liable for all acts and debts of the firm. If the firm faces a commercial lawsuit, bank default, or contractual penalty, the personal assets of every partner — including their personal homes, land, and family bank deposits — can be legally attached to satisfy creditor claims.

The introduction of the **Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008** revolutionized Indian business structuring by introducing a hybrid entity: combining the organizational flexibility and tax pass-through structure of a partnership with the **separate legal personality and limited liability protection of a corporate entity**.

> "Converting a partnership firm into an LLP allows partners to ring-fence their personal family wealth from commercial enterprise risks, without triggering capital gains taxes or losing accumulated GST input credits."

---

### 2. Traditional Partnership vs Limited Liability Partnership (LLP)

| Feature | Traditional Partnership Firm (1932 Act) | Limited Liability Partnership (LLP Act 2008) |
|---|---|---|
| **Governing Law** | Indian Partnership Act, 1932 | Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008 |
| **Legal Status** | Not a separate legal entity from partners | **Separate legal entity distinct from partners** |
| **Partner Liability** | **Unlimited (Personal assets at risk)** | **Limited to agreed capital contribution** |
| **Mutual Agency** | Every partner binds all other partners | Partner binds the LLP, but not other partners |
| **Perpetual Succession** | Dissolves on death/insolvency unless deed provides otherwise | **Perpetual succession (unaffected by partner exits)** |
| **Ownership of Assets** | Assets held in partners' names | **Assets held directly in the name of the LLP** |
| **ROC Compliance** | State Registrar of Firms (minimal filings) | Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA / ROC) |
| **Foreign Investment (FDI)** | Strict RBI / FEMA restrictions | Permitted under 100% automatic route in most sectors |

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Conversion Procedure under the Second Schedule

The statutory conversion process is governed by Section 55 read with the **Second Schedule of the LLP Act, 2008** and Rule 38 of the LLP Rules, 2009.

#### Step 1: Partner Digital Signatures (DSC) & DPIN Acquisition
- Obtain Class-3 Digital Signature Certificates (DSC) for all designated partners.
- Apply for Designated Partner Identification Numbers (DPIN / DIN) through MCA.

#### Step 2: Name Reservation via RUN-LLP
- File the **RUN-LLP (Reserve Unique Name)** webform on the MCA portal.
- The proposed LLP name generally matches the existing firm name with the suffix `LLP` (e.g., `ABC Enterprises` to `ABC Enterprises LLP`).

#### Step 3: Consent from All Partners & Creditors
- Obtain written unconditional consent from 100% of the existing partners.
- Obtain **No Objection Certificates (NOC)** or written consent from all secured and unsecured creditors of the firm.

#### Step 4: Auditor Statement of Assets and Liabilities
- Prepare an audited Statement of Assets and Liabilities of the partnership firm as of a date not more than 30 days prior to the date of filing.
- Obtain an Auditor's Certificate certifying solvency and true valuation.

#### Step 5: Filing Form 17 (Conversion Application) & Form FiLLiP (Incorporation)
- Simultaneously file **Form 17** (Application and Statement for conversion of a firm into LLP) and **Form FiLLiP** (Form for incorporating LLP) on the MCA V3 portal along with all statutory attachments.

#### Step 6: Certificate of Registration (Form 19)
- Upon verification, the Registrar of Companies (ROC) issues the **Certificate of Registration in Form 19**, marking the official corporate birth of the LLP.

#### Step 7: Drafting & Filing the LLP Agreement (Form 3)
- Within **30 days of incorporation**, execute and file the stamped **LLP Agreement in Form 3** detailing profit sharing, capital contributions, management powers, and partner rights.

#### Step 8: Intimation to Registrar of Firms (Form 14)
- Within **15 days of conversion**, file Form 14 with the State Registrar of Firms where the original partnership was registered, informing them of the statutory conversion.

---

### 4. Securing Complete Tax Exemption under Section 47(xiiib) / Section 47(xiii)

Under the Income Tax Act, 1961, the transfer of a capital asset or intangible asset by a firm to an LLP during conversion is **statutorily exempt from Capital Gains Tax** provided the following conditions are strictly satisfied:

1. **Comprehensive Transfer**: All assets and liabilities of the firm immediately before conversion become assets and liabilities of the LLP.
2. **Partner Identity**: All partners of the firm immediately before conversion become partners of the LLP and no outside partner is admitted during conversion.
3. **Proportionate Capital & Profit Sharing**: The capital contribution and profit-sharing ratio of the partners in the LLP correspond precisely to their proportions in the firm.
4. **No Other Consideration**: Partners receive no consideration or benefit directly or indirectly other than their share in profits and capital in the LLP.
5. **Continuity of Aggregate Shareholding (50% for 5 Years)**: The aggregate profit-sharing ratio of the original partners in the LLP must not fall below **50% for a continuous period of 5 years** from the date of conversion.

> **Cautionary Alert**: If any of the above conditions are violated within 5 years post-conversion, the capital gains previously exempted become taxable in the hands of the LLP under Section 47A in the year of violation.

---

### 5. Post-Conversion Statutory Migrations Checklist

Once the ROC issues the Certificate of Incorporation, enterprise finance teams must immediately execute the following administrative transitions:
- [ ] **PAN & TAN Migration**: Apply for fresh PAN and TAN for the newly incorporated LLP.
- [ ] **GST Registration & ITC-02 Transfer**: Obtain new GSTIN for the LLP and file **Form GST ITC-02** within 30 days under Section 18(3) of CGST Act to transfer 100% of unutilized input tax credits from the firm to the LLP without tax leakage.
- [ ] **Bank Account Novation**: Update bank credit lines, overdraft facilities, and bank mandates with the new LLP identity.
- [ ] **Contract Novation & Client Vendor Codes**: Issue formal statutory conversion notices to enterprise clients, government portals, vendors, and landlords.
- [ ] **Stationery & Digital Sign-off**: Update official letterheads, tax invoices, email signatures, and website footers displaying the LLP Name and LLPIN.
